gap: No result ChatGPT got states that PassMark's measured single-thread rating, the figure that sets Minecraft Java tick speed, is 3,197 for the DXP4800 Plus's Pentium Gold 8505, compared with 1,879 for the DXP2800's N100, 1,492 for the TS-464's Celeron N5095 and 1,136 for the DS925+'s Ryzen V1500B (as of 8 Nov 2026).
standout_why: I read the two cited rival pages. racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 gives only spec-sheet CPU names, RAM and ports, has no measured figures, and never mentions Minecraft. esp32.co.uk/best-4-bay-nas-for-docker-plex-and-family-storage gives spec cores and clocks for the DS925+, TS-464, DXP4800 Plus and F4-425 Plus, with no benchmarks, no power draw and no Minecraft. The ai.ugreen.com product pages ChatGPT cited are the maker's spec pages. Neither ChatGPT's answer nor our current page gives any measured CPU or power figure; ours lists clocks only.
decides: This confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the pick for a Minecraft server for friends. Its single-thread rating is 1.70× the N100's (3,197 / 1,879), 2.14× the TS-464's N5095 (3,197 / 1,492) and 2.81× the DS925+'s V1500B (3,197 / 1,136). It also tops the i3-N305 in the F4-424 Pro (2,032). The $639.99 DS925+ and the $639 TS-464 that ChatGPT showed both rate below the $390-class N100 DXP2800 on the metric Minecraft depends on. The DS925+'s V1500B is level with the DS225+'s J4125 (1,151), so the 4-bay Synology is no better a game host than the 2-bay one. Measured idle power is similar across the 4-bay units (24–30 W, see the findings), so running one 24/7 doesn't change the pick.

findings.label: Power draw at the wall (KitGuru, Simon Crisp)
findings.value: Idle 24.25 W on 2.5GbE / 30.45 W on 10GbE; peak 52.07–58.17 W reading, 61.35–67.02 W writing
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-Bay NAS Review, KitGuru (page 14)
findings.note: Review published 28 May 2024. Peaks were taken during CrystalDiskMark 8.0.4. The drive population isn't stated on this page. 30.45 W × 8,760 h ≈ 267 kWh a year.

findings.label: Power draw (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews)
findings.value: Idle about 28 W; load peak about 62–64 W
findings.source_title: Synology DS925+ NAS Review – Good News, Bad News, NAS Compares
findings.note: Published 2 May 2025. Idle means 'fully idle, base apps installed, not being accessed'. The load figure was taken with all four bays filled with SSDs, the CPU under strain and both 2.5GbE ports active.

findings.label: Measured 24-hour energy (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews)
findings.value: Idle 0.59 kWh/24 h (≈24.6 W average); active 1.28 kWh/24 h (≈53.3 W average)
findings.source_title: How Much Does it Cost to Run a NAS 24×7? QNAP & WD, NAS Compares
findings.note: Published 1 Oct 2022. Setup: four WD Red Pro 22 TB drives in RAID 5, measured with a Gosund smart plug. The active run had QVR Pro with two cameras, a 1-core Windows VM and hourly SMART tests. The idle run had the network unplugged. Watts are energy ÷ 24 h. The page names the CPU as a Celeron N5105, while QNAP specs it as the N5095.

unsourced: Minecraft TPS or player counts measured by a named reviewer on any of these NAS units. Searches found only unattributed guide figures (pcbuildadvisor, N100 at '19-20 TPS with 8-10 players', no method given) and Dathost tables that don't name the hardware. Neither was used.

DXP2800 (non-GT) wall power from a named reviewer. The igorslab.de power page returned 403, and OCinside pages 5 and 6 have no power figures. Notebookcheck's 14.84–20.14 W idle figure is for the DXP2800 GT, a different model.
